title: Tracing spiral arms in infrared
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 2090, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 2090 · constellation Columba · about 40 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #51 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Two curving, pale red spiral arms emerge from a shining central spot and each wraps once around this wide, oval galaxy, surrounded by a whirl of bright threads and dusty patches dotted with star formation. This is NGC 2090, about 40 million light-years away in Columba, in a combination of data from Webb's MIRI and NIRCam.

In visible light NGC 2090 looks flocculent, with a patchy, dusty disc and arms that seem flaky or vanish altogether. Webb's near-infrared camera brings those arms out clearly and also records starlight, shown in blue and strongest at the center. MIRI picks up mid-infrared light, shown in red, given off mainly by carbon-based molecules called polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons along the strands of gas and dust.

Hubble studied this galaxy early in its mission, tracking Cepheid variable stars to help refine the Hubble constant. That 1998 study put the galaxy at 37 million light-years. Newer measurements place it slightly farther.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.24 x 2.13 arcminutes) and distance (40 million light years), the frame spans roughly 26,000 × 25,000 light-years. Its light set out about 40 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Webb's NIRCam and MIRI combined near- and mid-infrared light. Blue shows starlight, cyan and green intermediate filters, and red the mid-infrared glow of PAH molecules in the dust.
understand.eye: This infrared light is invisible to the eye, and it reveals spiral arms that look flaky or invisible in visible-light images.

explore: NGC 2090 has long been a prominent nearby example of star formation. The Webb data come from program #3707, a census of massive star-forming galaxies at just the right distance for Webb to capture their tight star clusters and the gas clouds where stars can be born.
alt: A wide oval spiral galaxy with a bright center and two pale red arms each wrapping once around it, surrounded by bright threads and patches of dust, with foreground stars.
